producer_report.summary: Producer `cargo build`, `test`, `clippy` and `check` now take a build slot. The `athena` binary is linked as `cargo` in `<job_dir>/shim`. `producer_loop` puts that directory first on the producer's PATH only (`CargoShim` in env.rs); `env::build`, the verifier and the checks are unchanged. When `main` sees argv[0] == `cargo`, `slot_exec::run` finds the subcommand with the policy's shared `CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS` walk. `check_cargo` now uses the same walk, and its error text is unchanged. For the four building subcommands it takes a `Class::Producer` slot, runs the real cargo as a child with the shim removed from PATH, and frees the slot when cargo exits. `fmt`, `metadata`, `tree`, `doc`, `run` and unrecognised forms take no slot. The wrapper's wait is capped at half the Bash default timeout (300 s shipped), because the 1800 s `build_wait_s` would outlast the tool's call. After that wait the wrapper prints `no build slot free for <n> s; try again`, writes `<job_dir>/slot-wait.json`, exits 75 and never starts cargo. If the note is still there when the producer ends, `produce_and_verify` holds the job as `environment: build slot wait`. This retry fixes the earlier failures: `athena-cli --test slot_exec 8.00` is registered in xtask/shard-timings.txt, the fmt/metadata no-slot test is kept, and each criterion cites a runnable command. Also added: a CHANGELOG entry, design doc step 4 'Built' notes (including the argv[0] design instead of a `build-slot --` subcommand), and tests in the agent, core and cli crates.

open_issues: The final `cargo test --locked` returned without a failure exit code, but its output was too large to show and I could not open the saved copy (outside the working directory). Athena's own test run is the confirming check.

A job held at the producer stage keeps its `environment: build slot wait` marker after its retry lands, since only a consumed resume mark clears it. The pre-producer low-disk hold does the same. I left it: the retried-job guard stops a second retry, and changing hold lifecycle is outside this job. A later fix could clear a hold marker when its retry is dispatched.
A held producer run pays the producer's spend again on retry (no candidate to resume). This is stated in the design doc.

The wrapper's wait is capped at half the Bash default timeout (300 s shipped), shorter than design section 4's 1800 s. The design doc records the reason. If the agent passes a very short explicit Bash timeout, Bash can still end the call before the wrapper speaks.
A wrapper killed with SIGKILL frees its lock while its child cargo may still run briefly. Named in the design doc.
mistakes: My first core test asserted the old job's hold marker was cleared after the retry landed. It is not (no resume mark), so I removed that assertion and noted the behavior in open_issues.
A first version of the core env test read the shim link after the job's directory was cleaned. I fixed this by capturing the link inside the fake script.
The first clippy run failed on a complex test type (type_complexity); I replaced it with a type alias.
learnings: main.rs dispatches on argv[0] for the git hooks; a symlink named `cargo` to the athena binary reaches the same place, and std Command keeps the link path as argv[0].
Rust std opens files close-on-exec, so the real cargo child does not inherit the slot lock; the wrapper must stay alive holding it (no exec without unsafe).

A producer-stage SlotWait hold has no resume mark, so retry runs the producer from the base. The old job's hold marker is not cleared when its retry lands, because only a consumed resume mark clears it; the pre-producer disk hold behaves the same way.
athena.toml's Bash default timeout (600000 ms) is below the default build_wait_s (1800 s), so the wrapper's wait must be capped or the tool kills the call first.
Tests that read a job's directory after `go` finishes see it cleaned; capture what is needed inside the fake agent script.
